title: 45 mins of sheer panic : Lucky escape for many from Indirapuram towering infer
完整正文(原文):
GHAZIABAD: A fire ripped through five floors of a residential tower at a housing society in Indirapuram on Wednesday morning, burning down eight flats. Fortunately, around 20 people on the affected floors and in the flats were rescued on time. Around 10 people suffered minor injuries.
Most residents said they were getting ready for work or preparing to send their children to school when the blaze broke out on the ninth floor of Tower D of Gaur Green Avenue, which is at the first intersection of Indirapuram with NH-9, adjacent to the Delhi border.
Panic gripped floors seven through 13 for nearly 45 minutes. The ninth and 10th floors were worst affected — doors on both floors had jammed from the heat, leaving residents trapped and screaming for help till firefighters arrived and cut open the doors. To the world outside, the burning facade — visible from NH-9 and Hindon Elevated Road — became a spectacle for social media.
The fire department came in for criticism, with its initial efforts failing because the jet stream fell well short of the floors on fire. This meant valuable time was lost in controlling the blaze, which spread upwards and along the building’s facade. Gaur Green Avenue has 450 flats. Tower D has 110 apartments.
The fire department said it received the first distress call at 8.48 am and initially pressed five tenders into action. According to officials, the blaze originated in a 4BHK flat on the ninth floor that has been under renovation for five years. The flat is owned by Kamal Paliwal, who resides in another unit in the same building. Preliminary investigation points to a short circuit as the likely cause.
Fire department officials said Tower D was inaccessible to fire tenders at first due to a park boundary wall, because of which they had to park at a distance. Small tenders, which arrived first, also lacked the pressure to throw the jet stream high enough to reach the affected floors.
Chief fire officer Rahul Pai said his teams laid hose lines through the staircase up to the ninth floor, using the building’s fire suppression system as a starting point. “The fire was continuously spreading from the ninth floor upward, creating panic among residents trapped in their flats. Two teams were deployed to evacuate people via the staircases, while additional lines were laid using tenders from other fire stations to intensify firefighting efforts,” Pai said.
Twelve more fire tenders were subsequently called, including from Noida, along with two hydraulic platforms. Water from the fire tenders was used to replenish the society’s fire suppression system.
Pai admitted that the water didn’t reach the flames initially. “Within minutes, bigger fire engines of 22,000 and 14,000 litres capacity arrived. Small tenders navigate traffic faster, but bigger ones take longer — also because commuters on the road do not give way,” the CFO added. Firefighters, he said, broke more than 10 gates — iron and wooden — across five flats to reach trapped residents.
Kunjesh Singh Panwar, president of the apartment owners’ association, said the builder had handed over maintenance of the society about a decade ago. He pointed to the park built by the builder as a key factor in the delayed response. “Access to Block D is very limited because of the park, which is why fire tenders couldn’t reach on time,” he said.
A Gaurs Group spokesperson said the company was concerned about the incident and stood in solidarity with all affected residents. “Since the project was handed over, the AOA has been solely responsible for its management and operations,” the spokesperson said.
Panwar added that residents whose flats were damaged have been offered temporary accommodation by neighbours, and that the AOA was attending to all their needs.
Three people sustained injuries while manually activating the building’s fire suppression system. Resident Ajay Sharma of the eighth floor broke open the glass casing, pulled out the hose pipe and began dousing the fire himself. Society security guard Sonu did the same on the 10th floor. Fire department constable Randhawa Dhankad was also injured in the process. Others suffered minor injuries due to smoke inhalation.
Among those rescued was 80-year-old Mohammad Ayyub, who was on oxygen support and trapped on the 10th floor. Firefighters carried him down the stairs with his oxygen cylinder and rushed him to Medanta in Noida. On the ninth floor, 60-year-old Kusum Sharma, and on the 12th floor, 54-year-old Sarika Chaudhary, were both trapped after their doors jammed shut. Sharma was hospitalised.
Ruchi Sharma of flat 942 recalled that at around 8.30 am, a friend called to warn her about the fire in the flat directly opposite hers — just as she was preparing to send her children to school. When she opened her wooden door to check, she saw a wall of flames. “The fire was so intense that had my father not pulled me back, I would have been scorched,” she said.
Her mother took shelter in the bathroom with the water running, while Ruchi frantically called neighbours for help. The iron door had warped and jammed from the heat. “I tried to open the door with a towel, but it was impossible,” she said. The family remained trapped for nearly 45 minutes before firefighters cut through the door and rescued them. Their flat was gutted.
On the 10th floor, residents Ahmad, Pushpendra Sharma and Sandeep Pandey were also getting their children ready for school when smoke and flames rose from the flat below. They evacuated immediately, breaking their window with bricks and a stool to allow water to reach the fire inside.
The blaze was brought under control in approximately two hours by 70 fire personnel, using 17 tenders, water bowsers and two hydraulic platforms. Cooling operations continued for more than an hour after. Civil Defence, medical teams, police, SDRF and other administrative officials were present throughout and played a key role in coordinating the rescue.
Chief minister 
Yogi Adityanath took cognisance of the incident, after which district magistrate Ravinder Kumar Mandar reached the spot.
中文正文:
加济阿巴德：一栋住宅楼塔楼五层被大火吞噬，八套公寓被烧毁。幸运的是，受影响楼层和公寓内约20人被及时救出。约10人受轻伤。
大多数居民表示，火灾发生在高尔格林大道D座塔楼九楼时，他们正准备上班或送孩子上学。该小区位于因迪拉普拉姆与NH-9公路的第一个交叉口，毗邻德里边境。
7至13楼陷入恐慌近45分钟。9楼和10楼受灾最严重——两层楼的门都因高温变形卡住，居民被困呼救，直到消防员赶到破门而入。对外界来说，从NH-9公路和欣登高架路上都能看到的燃烧立面成为了社交媒体上的奇观。
消防部门受到批评，其最初的扑救努力失败，因为水柱远未达到着火楼层。这意味着控制火势损失了宝贵时间，火势向上蔓延并沿建筑立面扩散。高尔格林大道有450套公寓，D座有110套。
消防部门表示，上午8点48分接到第一个求救电话，最初出动了5辆消防车。据官员称，大火起源于9楼一套4BHK公寓，该公寓已装修五年。公寓业主卡迈勒·帕利瓦尔住在同一栋楼的另一单元。初步调查指向短路为可能原因。
消防部门官员表示，D座最初因公园围墙导致消防车无法接近，因此不得不停在远处。先到达的小型消防车也缺乏足够压力将水柱喷射到受影响楼层的高度。
首席消防官拉胡尔·帕伊说，他的团队通过楼梯铺设水带至9楼，以建筑的灭火系统为起点。"火势不断从9楼向上蔓延，使被困在公寓里的居民陷入恐慌。两队人员被部署通过楼梯疏散人员，同时调用其他消防站的消防车铺设更多水带以加强灭火力度，"帕伊说。
随后又调来了12辆消防车，包括从诺伊达调来的，以及两台液压平台。消防车的水被用来补充小区的灭火系统。
帕伊承认，最初水没有喷到火焰。"几分钟内，容量为22000升和14000升的大型消防车赶到。小型消防车穿越交通更快，但大型消防车需要更长时间——也因为路上的车辆不让行，"首席消防官补充说。他说，消防员在五套公寓中破开了超过10扇铁门和木门，以救出被困居民。
公寓业主协会主席昆杰什·辛格·帕瓦尔说，建筑商大约十年前就移交了小区的维护工作。他指出建筑商修建的公园是导致响应延迟的关键因素。"由于公园的存在，D座的通道非常有限，这就是消防车无法及时到达的原因，"他说。
高尔集团发言人表示，公司对这一事件表示关切，并与所有受影响居民站在一起。"自项目移交以来，公寓业主协会一直全权负责其管理和运营，"发言人说。
帕瓦尔补充说，公寓受损的居民已被邻居提供临时住所，协会正在满足他们的所有需求。
三人在手动启动建筑灭火系统时受伤。8楼居民阿贾伊·夏尔马打破玻璃外壳，拉出水管开始自己灭火。小区保安索努在10楼也做了同样的事。消防部门警员兰德哈瓦·丹卡德也在过程中受伤。其他人因吸入烟雾受轻伤。
被救出者包括80岁的穆罕默德·阿尤布，他靠氧气维持生命，被困在10楼。消防员带着他的氧气瓶把他抬下楼梯，紧急送往诺伊达的梅丹塔医院。9楼60岁的库苏姆·夏尔马和12楼54岁的萨里卡·乔杜里都因门卡住被困。夏尔马住院治疗。
942号公寓的鲁奇·夏尔马回忆说，上午8点30分左右，一位朋友打电话警告她对面公寓着火了——当时她正准备送孩子上学。当她打开木门查看时，看到一堵火墙。"火势太猛了，要不是我父亲把我拉回来，我就被烧焦了，"她说。
她母亲躲进浴室开着水龙头，鲁奇则疯狂地打电话向邻居求助。铁门因高温变形卡住。"我试着用毛巾开门，但根本不可能，"她说。一家人被困了近45分钟，直到消防员破门救出他们。他们的公寓被完全烧毁。
在10楼，居民艾哈迈德、普什彭德拉·夏尔马和桑迪普·潘迪也正准备送孩子上学，这时楼下公寓冒出浓烟和火焰。他们立即疏散，用砖块和凳子砸碎窗户，让水能喷到里面的火。
大火在约两小时内被70名消防人员控制，共使用17辆消防车、水罐车和两台液压平台。冷却作业持续了一个多小时。民防、医疗队、警察、国家灾害响应部队和其他行政官员全程在场，在协调救援中发挥了关键作用。
首席部长约吉·阿迪亚纳特注意到了这一事件，随后地区行政长官拉温德尔·库马尔·曼达尔赶到现场。

title: Fire breaks out on 7th floor of Atlantic Building in Mumbai Bandra West | Mumbai
完整正文(原文):
MUMBAI: A major fire broke out on the seventh floor of Atlantic Building on Sherly Rajan Road in Bandra West on Wednesday night, with one person feared trapped as firefighters battled to contain the blaze.
According to the Mumbai fire brigade, the incident was reported at 9. 12pm through the civic control room. Fire engines, police personnel, 108 ambulance services, Adani Electricity staff and ward officials were immediately rushed to the spot. The fire was upgraded to a Level-I incident at 9. 56pm.
The blaze engulfed the top floor of the ground-plus-seven-storey residential building within minutes, making access difficult for rescue teams. Locals said firefighters were struggling to reach the affected premises due to the intensity and spread of the flames. Reports from the spot suggested that one person may be trapped inside, although officials were yet to confirm the information.
Local corporator Swapna Mhatre of the BJP said the fire spread rapidly across the floor. “Several fire engines are at the site and personnel are working continuously to prevent the blaze from spreading further. 
However, the flames remain intense. Our immediate priority is to evacuate all residents safely,” she said.
Madhu Poplai of the Pali Hill Residents’ Association said the flames were visible from the upper floors of neighbouring buildings, triggering panic in the area. “The fire could be seen raging across the top flood of tha building, and residents watched in horror as the flames spread. We are hoping that no lives are lost and that the fire brigade is able to bring the situation under control quickly while rescuing anyone who may be trapped,” she said.
Firefighting operations were continuing late into the night. The cause of the fire was yet to be ascertained, and no official confirmation of casualties or injuries had been issued.
中文正文:
孟买：周三晚，班德拉西谢利·拉詹路大西洋大厦七楼发生重大火灾，消防员奋力扑救时，恐有一人被困。
据孟买消防队称，事件于晚上9点12分通过市政控制室报告。消防车、警察人员、108救护车服务、阿达尼电力公司工作人员和选区官员立即被派往现场。火灾于晚上9点56分升级为一级事件。
大火在几分钟内吞噬了这栋地上七层住宅楼的顶层，使救援队难以进入。当地居民说，由于火焰的强度和蔓延，消防员难以到达受影响区域。现场报告表明可能有一人被困在楼内，尽管官员尚未确认该信息。
当地人民党议员斯瓦普纳·哈特雷说，火势在整个楼层迅速蔓延。"数辆消防车在现场，人员正在持续工作以防止火势进一步蔓延。然而，火焰仍然很猛烈。我们的首要任务是安全疏散所有居民，"她说。
帕利山居民协会的马杜·波普莱说，从邻近建筑的高层可以看到火焰，引发了该地区的恐慌。"可以看到大火在建筑顶层肆虐，居民惊恐地看着火焰蔓延。我们希望没有生命损失，消防队能够迅速控制局势，同时救出任何可能被困的人，"她说。
灭火行动持续到深夜。火灾原因尚未确定，也没有官方确认伤亡情况。

title: Six injured in Riverdale apartment complex fire | The Riverdale Press
完整正文(原文):
At 10:03 a.m. Thursday, May 21, the New York Fire Department received a report of a fire at the Skyview apartment complex at 5900 Arlington Ave. in Riverdale.
Dozens of people, along with their pets and children, stood outside the building as fire personnel rushed inside.
The fire was reported on the eighth floor of the 23-story high rise residential building. The fire department said 21 units with 79 fire and EMS personnel were dispatched to fight the wind-driven blaze, which was brought under control at 11:19 a.m. Two civilians were injured, and one was taken to the hospital, according to the fire department.
Four firefighters suffered non-critical injuries, and three of them were transported to hospitals, the department said.
Brennah Cody, whose mother Dawn lives on the 20th floor, was among those first to witness the chaos that morning. The two had left the apartment for a doctor’s appointment when, on the way downstairs, they encountered smoke beginning to build in hallways and stairwells.
Cody recalled coming outside to hear screaming coming from an eight-floor window, where she saw residents “trapped and screaming for help.”
“Some people that were living in the apartment were like on their balconies, and were crouching down, trying to cover themselves” while firefighters broke the windows, said Cody. She said she immediately called 911.
Stu and Lori Kolinsky, who live on the 12th floor, said they saw the fire trucks arriving from their window, and received a message from building management instructing everyone above the seventh floor to evacuate. As they moved through the building, they encountered thick, black smoke they said they couldn’t see through.
“We had to get through the black, not knowing what was facing us when we opened the door,” Stu Kolinsky said.
Residents Betty and Jose Figueroa live on the building’s 17th floor. Betty Figueroa said she was on Zoom when she received the message from building management, which also urged residents to close doors behind them to prevent the spread of the fire.
When the Figueroas exited their apartment, the thick smoke raised concerns about Jose Figueroa’s preexisting respiratory condition. As a precautionary measure, Betty Figueroa rushed back into the apartment to retrieve two surgical masks.
“There was a lot of commotion, people were nervous — practically everyone on the phone,” Jose Figueroa said, describing the scene that greeted them once they reached the lobby.
Bennett Pologe, a resident of the building for 20 years, said he first noticed the smoke by its smell.
“It smelled sort of oddly sweet, I thought someone was cooking something a little disgusting.” He said. “And then suddenly, there’s a banging on my door.”
That banging was building staff, telling Pologe he had to leave the building immediately. He had time to grab his backpack with his laptop inside, but said his elderly neighbor left with “just the shirt on her back.”
Cody said the apartment where the fire sparked had been under renovation for some time. Several residents noted work was ongoing most weekdays and told The Press they witnessed construction workers on site the morning of the blaze.
Skyview management did not respond for comment by press time.
中文正文:
5月21日周四上午10点03分，纽约消防局接到报告，里弗代尔阿灵顿大道5900号Skyview公寓大楼发生火灾。
数十人带着他们的宠物和孩子站在楼外，消防人员冲进楼内。
火灾报告发生在这栋23层高层住宅楼的八楼。消防部门表示，派出了21个单位、79名消防和急救人员扑救这场被风助长的大火，火势于上午11点19分得到控制。消防部门称，两名平民受伤，其中一人被送往医院。
四名消防员受非危重伤，其中三人被送往医院。
布伦娜·科迪的母亲唐恩住在20楼，她是当天早上最早目睹混乱场面的人之一。两人离开公寓去看医生，在下楼途中遇到走廊和楼梯间开始积聚的烟雾。
科迪回忆说，走到外面后听到八楼一扇窗户传来尖叫声，她看到居民"被困并尖叫求救"。
"一些住在公寓里的人在阳台上，蹲下来试图掩护自己"，同时消防员打破窗户，科迪说。她说她立即拨打了911。
住在12楼的斯图和洛里·科林斯基说，他们从窗户看到消防车到达，并收到大楼管理部门的消息，指示七楼以上的所有人疏散。穿过大楼时，他们遇到了浓黑的烟雾，说根本看不见。
"我们必须穿过黑暗，不知道开门时会面对什么，"斯图·科林斯基说。
居民贝蒂和何塞·菲格罗亚住在大楼17楼。贝蒂·菲格罗亚说，她正在开Zoom会议时收到了大楼管理部门的消息，消息还敦促居民随手关门以防止火势蔓延。
菲格罗亚夫妇离开公寓时，浓烟引发了对何塞·菲格罗亚既往呼吸系统疾病的担忧。作为预防措施，贝蒂·菲格罗亚冲回公寓取了两个医用口罩。
"场面很混乱，人们很紧张——几乎每个人都在打电话，"何塞·菲格罗亚描述他们到达大堂时看到的场景说。
在这栋楼住了20年的居民贝内特·波洛格说，他首先是通过气味注意到烟雾的。
"闻起来有点奇怪的甜味，我以为有人在做什么有点恶心的东西。"他说。"然后突然，有人砸我的门。"
砸门的是大楼工作人员，告诉波洛格必须立即离开大楼。他有时间抓起装着笔记本电脑的背包，但说他的老年邻居"只穿着身上的衬衫"就离开了。
科迪说，起火的那套公寓已经装修了一段时间。几位居民指出，大多数工作日都在施工，并告诉《新闻报》他们在火灾当天早上看到建筑工人在现场。
截至发稿时，Skyview管理层未回应置评请求。

title: Two killed in Nha Trang apartment complex fire - VnExpress International
完整正文(原文):
The blaze erupted around 4 p.m. in a 50-square-meter unit at a 26-story residential complex on To Hieu Street, located near the beach in Nam Nha Trang Ward of Khanh Hoa Province. The fire reportedly started in the bedroom, where a mattress, blankets, and other flammable items fueled its rapid spread.
Thick black smoke filled the corridor and rose to the upper floors, triggering alarms and forcing panicked residents to evacuate via the staircases. From the street, a large column of smoke was visible rising above the complex, which consists of three towers and over 1,000 apartments.
Le Thanh Hoa, a resident on the 16th floor, said she and her neighbors alerted authorities and fled immediately after seeing flames engulf the nearby unit.
Khanh Hoa Province fire and rescue police deployed 36 officers, two ladder trucks, and three fire engines to the scene. Firefighters accessed the burning unit through a neighboring apartment to contain the spread while guiding residents to safety. The fire was brought under control within 30 minutes.
Nguyen Thanh Ha, Vice Chairman of the Khanh Hoa People’s Committee, confirmed that a man and a woman were killed. Their bodies were discovered in the bedroom, where the fire had caused significant damage.
According to a building management representative, neighbors heard arguing coming from the apartment prior to the fire. Because the door was locked, management staff had to force entry and use portable extinguishers in an initial attempt to fight the blaze.
Police completed their examination of the scene by 8:30 p.m.
The victims’ bodies were transferred to Khanh Hoa General Hospital for autopsies. Authorities have not yet released the identities of the victims or the official cause of the fire.
中文正文:
大火于下午4点左右在庆和省芽庄南区临海的苏氏孝街一栋26层住宅楼的一套50平方米单元内爆发。据报道，火灾始于卧室，床垫、毯子和其他易燃物品助长了火势的迅速蔓延。
浓浓的黑烟充满走廊并上升到高层，触发警报，迫使惊慌的居民通过楼梯疏散。从街上可以看到巨大的烟柱从该小区上方升起，该小区由三座塔楼和1000多套公寓组成。
16楼居民黎清花说，她和邻居看到火焰吞噬附近单元后立即报警并逃离。
庆和省消防救援警察部署了36名人员、两辆云梯车和三辆消防车到现场。消防员通过邻近公寓进入起火单元以控制蔓延，同时引导居民到安全地带。火势在30分钟内得到控制。
庆和省人民委员会副主席阮清河确认，一名男子和一名女子死亡。他们的尸体在卧室被发现，那里火灾造成了严重损坏。

title: Kind stirbt bei Feuer in Berliner Hochhaus : Nachbarn h?rten Schreie
完整正文(原文):
Merz und Merkel bedroht — Staatsanwaltschaft ermittelt gegen Kabarettist Uwe Steimle
Baby stirbt bei Hochhaus-Brand in Berlin: Nachbarn hörten Schreie: „Ich brauche Hilfe!“
Feuer entstand offenbar in Messie-Wohnung
Berlin-Friedrichsfelde – Eine Feuerkatastrophe in einem 21-stöckigen Hochhaus in Berlin-Friedrichsfelde hat ein Kind das Leben gekostet, zwei Menschen sind in einem kritischen Zustand. Jetzt gibt es Details dazu, wo das Feuer am Mittwochabend um kurz vor 20 Uhr ausgebrochen ist.
Bei der Brandwohnung im dritten Stock soll es sich nach Angaben der Feuerwehr um ein Apartment handeln, in dem sich ungewöhnlich viele Gegenstände und Möbel befanden – offenbar eine Messie-Wohnung. Das Feuer breitete sich rasant aus, die Unordnung erschwerte die Löscharbeiten erheblich.
Der 75 Jahre alte Bewohner der Wohnung konnte sich retten, liegt jetzt im Krankenhaus. Viele andere Hausbewohner flüchteten ebenfalls, andere wählten den Notruf oder machten an den Fenstern auf sich aufmerksam. Feuerwehrtrupps führten sie durch das Treppenhaus nach draußen.
Mutter und zwei Kinder bewusstlos aufgefunden
Im Hausflur der vierten Etage aber fanden die Einsatzkräfte drei bewusstlose Personen. Nach Polizeiangaben handelt es sich um eine 26-Jährige und ihre beiden Kinder im Alter von 5 Jahren und neun Monaten. Laut Feuerwehr wurden alle drei noch auf der Fahrt ins Krankenhaus von Notärzten reanimiert. Das Baby, nach BILD-Informationen ein Junge, starb in der Klinik. Die Frau und der Fünfjährige „befinden sich weiterhin in einem kritischen Zustand“, so ein Polizeisprecher.
Howoge-Geschäftsführer Ulrich Schiller sagte zu dem Feuer im Hochhaus der Wohnungsbaugesellschaft: „Wir trauern mit der Familie und können den Schmerz über den Tod des Kindes kaum in Worte fassen.“
Nachbar hörte Frau schreien
Zainuddin Zahin (41) lebt mit seiner Frau und seinen drei Söhnen (4 Monate, 6 und 8) im 4. Stock des Feuerhauses – er berichtet: „Ich habe um 19.20 Uhr mein Auto unten geparkt und bin durch den Flur hoch zu unserer Wohnung. Da habe ich schon einen komischen Geruch bemerkt. Ich habe meine Frau gefragt, ob sie gekocht hat und etwas angebrannt ist. Von draußen haben wir plötzlich Geschrei gehört. Als ich die Wohnungstür wieder geöffnet habe, war alles voll Rauch. Aus der Wohnung meiner vietnamesischen Nachbarn, habe ich die Frau schreien hören: Ich brauche Hilfe, ich brauche Hilfe! Ich habe Polizei und Feuerwehr Bescheid gegeben. Aber es war wohl zu spät. Das Kind ist tot.“
Bewohnerin Minhthu Wu (43) zu BILD: „In den anderen Stockwerken ging der Rauchmelder an. Wir wollten erst aus dem Haus, aber haben durch den Spion gesehen, dass das ganze Treppenhaus voll Rauch ist. Wir hatten Angst vor einer Rauchvergiftung. Wir haben alles zugemacht, nasse Lappen vor die Türen gelegt.“ Die Einsatzkräfte kontrollierten rund 60 Wohnungen. Einsturzgefährdet ist das Haus nicht, die Polizei ermittelt nun zur Brandursache. Bewohner Zhain: Wir dürfen aktuell nicht in unsere Wohnung, wissen nicht, wie es darin aussieht, ob es nur verraucht ist oder schlimmer. Wir sind bis mindestens Samstag im Hotel untergebracht.“
170 Feuerwehrleute waren im Großeinsatz. Unter Atemschutz holten sie 70 Menschen aus dem verqualmten Gebäude und brachten sie in Sicherheit. Insgesamt kamen sieben Menschen in Krankenhäuser. 21 Wohnungen sind laut Howoge am Donnerstag noch „polizeilich gesperrt“. Die Stromversorgung im Gebäude sei gewährleistet, einige Heizungen aber noch abgestellt. Der Aufzug sei noch außer Betrieb, Techniker seien dabei, ihn schnellstmöglich wieder in Betrieb zu nehmen.
Bezirk organisiert Notunterkünfte für Bewohner
Viele Bewohner mussten zunächst anderswo unterkommen. Wer nicht bei Verwandten oder Bekannten bleiben konnte, schlief in einer nahegelegenen Turnhalle. Der Bezirk bemühe sich, für die Zeit danach Wohnungen und Hotels zu organisieren, wie es hieß.

中文正文:
柏林高层火灾中婴儿死亡：邻居听到尖叫："我需要帮助！"
火灾显然发生在囤积者公寓
柏林-弗里德里希斯费尔德——柏林-弗里德里希斯费尔德一栋21层高层住宅发生火灾灾难，造成一名儿童死亡，两人情况危急。现在有了关于周三晚上近8点火灾发生地点的详细信息。
据消防部门称，三楼的起火公寓是一套里面有异常多物品和家具的公寓——显然是一间囤积者公寓。火势迅速蔓延，杂乱的物品严重阻碍了灭火工作。
这套公寓的75岁住户设法逃生，目前在医院。许多其他居民也逃离了，其他人拨打了紧急电话或在窗户旁引起注意。消防队带领他们穿过楼梯间到外面。
母亲和两个孩子被发现失去意识
然而，救援人员在四楼的走廊里发现了三名失去意识的人。据警方称，是一名26岁妇女和她两个分别为5岁和9个月大的孩子。据消防部门称，三人在送往医院的途中都被急救医生复苏。据《图片报》信息，婴儿是一名男孩，在医院死亡。警方发言人说，该妇女和5岁儿童"仍处于危急状态"。
住房公司Howoge总经理乌尔里希·席勒谈到这栋高层住宅的火灾时说："我们与这家人一起哀悼，几乎无法用语言表达对孩子死亡的悲痛。"
邻居听到妇女尖叫
扎因丁·扎欣（41岁）和妻子及三个儿子（4个月、6岁和8岁）住在起火建筑的四楼——他报告说："我在19点20分把车停在下面，穿过走廊上楼回我们的公寓。那时我已经注意到一种奇怪的气味。我问我妻子是不是她做饭烧糊了什么。我们突然听到外面有尖叫声。当我再次打开公寓门时，到处都是烟。从我越南邻居的公寓里，我听到那个女人在喊：我需要帮助，我需要帮助！我通知了警察和消防队。但可能已经太晚了。孩子死了。"
居民明图·吴（43岁）对《图片报》说："其他楼层的烟雾报警器响了。我们起初想出去，但通过猫眼看到整个楼梯间都是烟。我们害怕烟雾中毒。我们把所有东西都关上了，把湿布放在门前。"救援人员检查了约60套公寓。建筑没有倒塌危险，警方目前正在调查火灾原因。居民扎欣说：我们目前不能进公寓，不知道里面怎么样，是只有烟熏还是更糟。我们至少到周六都住在酒店。"
170名消防员参与了大规模行动。他们佩戴呼吸器从充满烟雾的建筑中救出70人并带到安全地带。共有7人被送往医院。据Howoge称，周四仍有21套公寓"被警方封锁"。建筑的电力供应已得到保障，但一些暖气仍被关闭。电梯仍在停运中，技术人员正在努力尽快恢复运行。
区政府为居民组织紧急住所
许多居民最初不得不在别处落脚。不能住在亲戚或朋友家的人睡在附近的体育馆。据称，区政府正在努力为之后的时间组织公寓和酒店。

title: 刻不容缓 ！ 一场与时间赛跑的紧急救援 -- 中国警察网
完整正文(原文): 10月23日凌晨，按照安徽省马鞍山市公安局花山分局常态化夜间巡防部署，绿地警务站民警潘小虎与辅警张文龙沿朝霞路开展巡逻值守。行至某居民小区附近时，潘小虎凭借多年夜巡积累的敏锐洞察力，发现临街一栋高层住宅楼20多层处有异常火光闪烁。 因高层建筑遮挡，无法锁定起火楼层，二人当即分工：潘小虎前往小区，同步向上级详细汇报火情位置、现场火势等实时动态；张文龙紧随其后，在小区入口做好秩序维护与引导准备。 “不确定火源，就从20层开始逐层排查！”面对紧急态势，二人迅速敲定方案，沿楼梯从20层开始逐层向上排查。随着排查推进，空气中的焦糊味愈发浓烈。当二人排查至25层时，一股刺鼻浓烟从一户居民家门缝渗出，起火点找到了！ 潘小虎一边向指挥中心上报起火点准确地址，请求支援警力及消防力量紧急驰援，一边与张文龙轮番用力敲打起火住户房门。“屋里有人吗？着火了，快开门！”急促的呼叫声与敲门声在空旷的楼道内回荡，屋内却始终无人回应。 因房门为加固结构，二人尝试撬动、撞击均无法打开。情况愈发紧急，潘小虎继续在门外呼喊提醒，张文龙则迅速逐户敲门，引导25层及以上住户有序向楼下安全区域疏散。 随后，花山分局特巡警大队、霍里派出所警力接到指挥中心支援指令后迅速响应，火速抵达现场，共同疏导住户30余人，并同步引导消防救援车、120急救车顺利入场。很快，消防救援力量与120急救人员相继赶到。 消防救援人员使用破拆工具打开起火房门，浓烟与热浪瞬间涌出。消防救援人员迅速展开灭火救援，仅用10分钟便成功控制住火势，并救出被困在卧室内的谷先生一家四口，其中包括一名年仅1岁的幼儿。经120急救人员初步检查，4人虽吸入少量浓烟，但意识清醒，随后被紧急送往医院做进一步观察。 “当晚家中用电饭锅炖煮排骨后忘记关闭电源，全家睡着后未察觉异常，连门外的救援呼喊和敲门声都没听见。”事后，谷先生回忆事发经过时仍心有余悸。参与救援的消防救援人员表示，凌晨时段是居民熟睡、安全防范意识最薄弱的时期，若火情未被及时发现，待火势与浓烟大范围蔓延后，极可能造成无法挽回的后果。睡前要仔细检查相关电器、煤气灶是否关闭。 据悉，花山分局科学规划16条夜间警力必巡路线，在重点商圈、居民小区、交通要道设置12个必守点位，通过“定点值守+动态巡逻”的常态化模式，全力守护群众安全。 “花山分局通过夜间巡防工作筑牢辖区治安防线，全力守护群众生命财产安全。”花山分局副局长张阅表示。据统计，今年以来，该局通过夜间巡防累计及时发现并处置各类安全隐患146起，协助侦破案件149起，为群众办实事、解难题890余次。

title: Woman dies , niece injured in Vile Parle flat fire
完整正文(原文):
Woman dies, niece injured in Vile Parle flat fire
The two women were visiting their family living in the building for wedding-related rituals when the incident occurred, residents said
Mumbai: A 62-year-old woman died, and her 34-year-old niece was injured in a fire that broke out in a flat in a 13-storey residential building in Vile Parle East on Monday, casting a pall over a family preparing for a wedding scheduled for the following day.
The deceased has been identified as Bhavana Satra, the sister-in-law of the groom’s father, who owned the flat in which the fire broke out. Her niece, identified as Aneree Satra, is undergoing treatment at Nanavati Hospital with 6% burns and is reported to be stable. The two women were visiting their family living in the building for wedding-related rituals when the incident occurred, residents said.
Fire officials said the cause of the Level-1 (small) blaze is yet to be ascertained, and a detailed investigation has been initiated.
The incident occurred in a flat on the 13th and topmost floor of Suvidha Pearl, a residential building on Pheroze Shah Mehta Road, at around 9.51 am, officials from the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation’s disaster management department said.
According to residents, a religious ritual was underway in the flat earlier in the day, which involved a small ceremonial pyre. The family later went down to the seventh floor for breakfast, when neighbours alerted them to smoke billowing from the apartment. Bhavana and Aneree Satra rushed back to the 13th-floor flat along with two others.
When they opened the main door, the fire suddenly intensified, releasing dense smoke into the corridor and common areas. While the others managed to flee towards the staircase, Bhavana Satra, an asthma patient, collapsed near a duct and lost consciousness. She suffered severe smoke inhalation and burn injuries, and later succumbed. It remains unclear how Aneree Satra sustained burn injuries.
After the Mumbai Fire Brigade was alerted about the fire, firefighters rushed to the spot with five fire engines and two jumbo water tankers. Firefighters faced difficulties as thick smoke had filled the corridor and stairwell, particularly because the flat was on the top floor, officials said. The blaze was brought under control by around 1.44 pm.
Both women were taken to Nanavati Hospital, where Bhavana Satra was declared dead on arrival. A relative of the bride said the family was considering postponing the wedding in view of the tragedy.

维尔帕勒公寓火灾造成一名妇女死亡，侄女受伤
居民说，事件发生时，两名妇女正在拜访住在楼里的家人，参加婚礼相关仪式
孟买：周一，维尔帕勒东一栋13层住宅楼的一套公寓发生火灾，一名62岁妇女死亡，她34岁的侄女受伤，给一个正准备第二天婚礼的家庭蒙上了阴影。
死者被确认为巴瓦娜·萨特拉，是新郎父亲的嫂子，新郎父亲拥有发生火灾的公寓。她的侄女被确认为阿内里·萨特拉，正在纳米瓦蒂医院接受6%烧伤的治疗，据报道情况稳定。居民说，事件发生时，两名妇女正在拜访住在楼里的家人，参加婚礼相关仪式。
消防官员说，这场一级（小型）火灾的原因尚待确定，已展开详细调查。
布里汉孟买市政公司灾害管理部门的官员说，事件发生在上午9点51分左右，地点是菲罗兹·沙·梅塔路住宅楼苏维达·珀尔的13楼（顶层）公寓。
据居民说，当天早些时候公寓里正在进行一个宗教仪式，涉及一个小型祭祀火堆。家人后来下到七楼吃早餐，这时邻居提醒他们公寓冒出浓烟。巴瓦娜和阿内里·萨特拉与另外两人一起冲回13楼公寓。
当他们打开主门时，火势突然加剧，向走廊和公共区域释放浓烟。其他人设法逃向楼梯时，患有哮喘的巴瓦娜·萨特拉在一个管道附近倒下并失去意识。她遭受严重烟雾吸入和烧伤，后来不治身亡。目前尚不清楚阿内里·萨特拉是如何遭受烧伤的。
孟买消防队接到火灾警报后，消防员带着五辆消防车和两辆巨型水罐车紧急赶到现场。官员说，由于浓烟充满走廊和楼梯间，消防员面临困难，特别是因为公寓在顶层。火势在下午1点44分左右得到控制。
两名妇女都被送往纳米瓦蒂医院，巴瓦娜·萨特拉在到达时被宣布死亡。新娘的一位亲戚说，鉴于这场悲剧，家人正在考虑推迟婚礼。

title: Fierce Fire Sweeps 38 - Storey Condo In Bangkok , Multiple Occupants Trapped
完整正文(原文):
BANGKOK – A violent fire tore through a 38-storey luxury condominium in Bangkok’s busy Pinklao district on Thursday afternoon, sending columns of black smoke into the sky and trapping residents on higher floors.
The blaze, which started on the 16th floor opposite CentralPlaza Pinklao, has sharpened scrutiny of fire safety in the capital’s packed high-rises. The first alarm came at about 1:55 p.m., after flames broke out inside a unit on the 16th floor of the tower on Somdet Phra Pinklao Road in Arun Amarin, Bangkok Noi.
Witnesses described a terrifying scene as thick, choking smoke burst from shattered windows and climbed the facade within minutes. “It looked like the side of the tower was spewing smoke,” said Somchai Wong, 45, who had been shopping at the nearby mall. “People were crying out from balconies and waving cloths. You could hear the fear.”
Home to more than 500 units, the modern riverside condo houses families, young professionals, and expatriates drawn to the Chao Phraya views. It became a vertical trap as the fire spread. Crews from Bang Pla Thanon Fire Station and Bangkok Noi rescue teams arrived quickly with more than a dozen engines and ladder trucks.
The flames, fed by furnishings and possibly faulty wiring, proved stubborn. Smoke moved through vents and corridors, turning stairwells into hazards. Many residents sheltered in hallways or on balconies while waiting to be reached.
At least 20 people were cut off above the source of the fire, surrounded by smoke that blocked exits. Videos on social media showed a mother on the 22nd floor clutching a toddler as smoke seeped under a door, and an older couple on the 28th floor struggling to breathe while firefighters raced to position a rescue basket.
“We could not see ahead of us,” said survivor Nattaporn Lee, 32, who escaped from the 15th floor with burns on her arms. “The lifts were shut, the stairs were full of dark smoke. I thought we would not make it.” Some residents tried to knot bedsheets into ropes, though most were escorted down by firefighters with breathing gear or brought down by aerial platforms.
CentralPlaza Pinklao Was partly Evacuated
By 4:30 p.m., after roughly three hours, firefighters had confined the blaze to floors 16 to 20. The fire chief said the structure remained sound, although upper floors were not safe to occupy. Early checks suggest an air conditioning short-circuit may have sparked the fire, but forensic teams are still combing the site.
No deaths have been confirmed, a stroke of luck, though 15 people were taken to Siriraj Hospital and Phramongkutklao Hospital with smoke inhalation and minor injuries. CentralPlaza Pinklao was partly evacuated, with cinemas and shops closed for several hours as drifting embers raised concern.
The incident adds to a list of serious fires that have haunted Bangkok. Weak oversight and ageing systems have often turned buildings into risks. The 1993 Kader Toy Factory blaze in Nakhon Pathom remains the country’s worst industrial fire, with 188 dead after locked exits and collapsing steel frames trapped workers.
In 2009, fireworks ignited flammable decor at the Santika Pub in Ekkamai, killing 67 people at a New Year’s event and exposing substandard controls, including too few extinguishers for a crowded venue. In December 2024, a fire at The Ember Hotel near Khao San Road killed three foreign tourists, with survivors fleeing upwards amid broken windows and delays.
State Tower and Grand Park Avenue Hotel Fires
In March 2012, fires at the State Tower and Grand Park Avenue Hotel revealed breaches of building rules, such as poor fire escapes and overloaded wiring.
These events highlight a long-running risk across a skyline of more than 5,000 towers, including condominiums, offices, and hotels. Heat and humidity raise the chance of electrical faults. Experts say buildings approved after 1992 must meet the Building Control Act requirements, including sprinklers, pressurized stairwells, and yearly checks by qualified engineers.
However, enforcement has been inconsistent. The 1997 Ministerial Regulation No. 47 allows the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration to require upgrades in older properties, such as improved fire escapes and smoke detectors in every unit. A 2016 Bangkok Post report found only 40 percent of pre-1992 towers received regular audits, leaving many residents at risk.
“Smoke spreads quicker than flames in these towers because of open facades and poor sealing,” said Dr Supachai Tangwongsan, a fire safety engineer at Chulalongkorn University. “Many condos lack proper compartment walls to slow fire, and some keep faulty wiring.
With rapid growth, inspection often falls behind.” He noted the 1997 Royal Jomtien Resort Hotel fire, where a propane leak killed 100 people and injured many more. A later review in the province found hundreds of buildings out of compliance.
Bangkok Governor Orders Inspections
The pattern has not gone away. A 2023 Savills report on high-rises in Southeast Asia warned that design choices in Thailand often favour looks over clear escape routes and safe ground-level evacuation areas.
Following Thursday’s blaze, BMA Governor Chadchart Sittipunt ordered immediate inspections of condominiums in the Pinklao area. He promised fines for violations and support for safety upgrades.
“We have come too close to disaster before,” he said at a briefing outside the cordon, as residents covered in soot waited under tents. The Thailand Fire Safety Network urged mandatory evacuation drills and alarms linked to authorities in real time.
For families displaced to temporary shelters at the mall, the shock was plain. “We chose this place for the view, not the vents,” said resident Aree Jiranunt, 28, holding her singed cat. As crews cleared debris at sunset, Bangkok looked to answers and action. In a city of soaring towers, keeping people safe from smoke and fire has never felt more urgent.
中文正文:
曼谷——周四下午，一场猛烈的火灾席卷了曼谷繁忙的平桥区一栋38层豪华公寓楼，黑烟柱升入天空，高层居民被困。
大火始于中央广场平桥对面的16楼，加剧了人们对首都密集高层建筑消防安全的审视。第一次警报在下午1点55分左右传来，此前火焰在曼谷诺伊阿伦阿玛林颂德拍平桥路塔楼16楼的一套单元内爆发。
目击者描述了可怕的场景，令人窒息的浓烟从破碎的窗户喷出，几分钟内就爬上了立面。"看起来塔楼侧面在喷烟，"45岁的颂猜·旺说，他一直在附近的商场购物。"人们在阳台上哭喊，挥舞着布。你能听到恐惧。"
这栋现代河畔公寓拥有500多个单元，住着被湄南河景色吸引的家庭、年轻专业人士和外籍人士。随着火势蔓延，它变成了一个垂直陷阱。邦帕拉坦消防局和曼谷诺伊救援队的人员带着十几辆消防车和云梯车迅速到达。
火焰由家具和可能的故障线路助燃，证明难以扑灭。烟雾通过通风口和走廊移动，使楼梯间变成危险区域。许多居民在走廊或阳台上避难，等待救援。
至少20人被切断在火源上方，被阻挡出口的烟雾包围。社交媒体上的视频显示，22楼一位母亲抱着一个蹒跚学步的孩子，烟雾从门下渗入；28楼一对老年夫妇呼吸困难，消防员竞相定位救援篮。
"我们看不见前方，"32岁的幸存者纳塔蓬·李说，她从15楼逃出，手臂有烧伤。"电梯关了，楼梯里全是黑烟。我以为我们出不去了。"一些居民试图把床单结成绳子，不过大多数人由佩戴呼吸装备的消防员护送下来，或由空中平台接下。
中央广场平桥部分疏散
到下午4点30分，大约三小时后，消防员将火势限制在16至20楼。消防局长说建筑结构仍然完好，不过高层不安全居住。初步检查表明空调短路可能引发了火灾，但法医团队仍在现场排查。
没有确认死亡，算是幸运，不过15人因烟雾吸入和轻伤被送往西里拉医院和帕蒙固告医院。中央广场平桥部分疏散，电影院和商店关闭了数小时，因为飘移的余烬引发担忧。
这一事件增加了困扰曼谷的一系列严重火灾。薄弱的监管和老化的系统经常使建筑变成风险。1993年佛统府卡德玩具厂大火仍是该国最严重的工业火灾，锁闭的出口和坍塌的钢架困住工人，造成188人死亡。
2009年，烟花在埃卡迈的桑蒂卡酒吧点燃了易燃装饰，在新年活动中造成67人死亡，暴露了不合标准的管控，包括拥挤场所灭火器过少。2024年12月，考山路附近的恩伯酒店火灾造成三名外国游客死亡，幸存者在破碎的窗户和延误中向上逃离。
国家大厦和公园大道酒店火灾
2012年3月，国家大厦和公园大道酒店的火灾暴露了建筑规则的违反，如消防通道差和线路过载。
这些事件凸显了拥有5000多座塔楼（包括公寓、办公楼和酒店）的天际线长期存在的风险。高温和湿度增加了电气故障的几率。专家说，1992年后获批的建筑必须符合《建筑控制法》要求，包括喷淋系统、加压楼梯间和合格工程师的年度检查。
然而，执法一直不一致。1997年第47号部长条例允许曼谷市政当局要求对旧物业进行升级，如改进消防通道和每个单元安装烟雾探测器。2016年《曼谷邮报》的一篇报道发现，1992年前的塔楼中只有40%接受了定期审计，使许多居民处于风险之中。
"在这些塔楼中，烟比火蔓延得更快，因为立面开放和密封差，"朱拉隆功大学消防安全工程师素帕猜·坦旺桑博士说。"许多公寓缺乏适当的隔墙来减缓火势，有些还保留着故障线路。随着快速增长，检查往往跟不上。"他提到了1997年皇家乔木提恩度假酒店火灾，丙烷泄漏造成100人死亡，更多人受伤。该省后来的审查发现数百栋建筑不合规。
曼谷市长下令检查
这种模式没有消失。2023年第一太平戴维斯关于东南亚高层建筑的报告警告说，泰国的设计选择往往偏爱外观，而不是清晰的逃生路线和安全的地面疏散区域。
周四大火后，曼谷市长查查特·西蒂蓬下令立即检查平桥区的公寓楼。他承诺对违规行为处以罚款，并支持安全升级。
"我们之前已经太接近灾难了，"他在警戒线外的简报会上说，满身烟灰的居民在帐篷下等待。泰国消防安全网络敦促强制进行疏散演练和与当局实时连接的警报。
对于被转移到商场临时庇护所的家庭来说，震惊是显而易见的。"我们选择这个地方是为了景色，不是为了通风口，"28岁的居民阿里·吉拉南抱着她被烧焦的猫说。随着救援人员在日落时清理废墟，曼谷期待着答案和行动。在一座塔楼林立的城市里，保护人们免受烟雾和火灾的伤害从未显得如此紧迫。

title: 记者直击 ： 香港大埔大火已造成44人遇难 ， 有老者称  住了几十年 ， 没见过这么大的火  |火场|消防处
完整正文(原文):
经济观察报记者 郑晨烨
11月27日凌晨3时57分，香港特区政府发布新闻公报，通报大埔宏福苑五级火警的最新伤亡数据：事故已造成36人死亡，36人受伤，其中7人情况危殆。在确认的死者中，包含一名入职9年的消防队员，仍有279人处于失联状态。
另据最新信息，大埔宏福苑火灾目前已造成44人遇难，45人受伤。香港警方已拘捕3名相关工程公司负责人，包括2名董事、1名工程顾问，年龄介于52岁至68岁。
这场大火始于11月26日下午2时51分，起火点最初位于宏昌阁外墙棚架，随后火势在数小时内迅速蔓延至周边大厦，于当日傍晚6时22分被消防处升级为香港火警分级制度中最高的“五级”。
香港特区行政长官李家超在27日凌晨的记者会上，将此次事件定性为“重大灾难”。
11月27日凌晨1点，经济观察报记者赶抵大埔事发现场。
通往宏福苑的周边道路已被警方实施大范围交通管制，出租车司机告诉记者“附近四十几条路已全部封死”，大量消防车、救护车及警车停满了街道。
虽然警戒线被拉设在距离火场较远的位置，但记者在封锁线外仍能闻到空气中弥漫着浓烈的焦煳味，地面上散落着大量被风吹至此处的、呈黑色的颗粒状崩落物。
透过夜色，记者在现场看到，宏福苑西北方向楼宇的明火已基本熄灭，但东南方向的三栋大厦外立面仍有明火燃烧，部分中高楼层的窗户内透出清晰的红光。
警方在通报中指出，此次火势蔓延速度及程度“不寻常”，目前已联同消防处成立专案组，明确循刑事方向展开全方位调查。
封锁线外，地面上呈黑色的颗粒状崩落物 郑晨烨/摄
11月27日凌晨2点，部分楼栋外立面火势仍明显 郑晨烨/摄
凌晨的大埔
11月27日凌晨1时，经济观察报记者抵达香港大埔宏福苑火灾现场，此时，距离起火已过去逾10个小时。
由于火势仍未完全扑灭，警方在距离事发屋苑数个街区外拉起了多重封锁线。
据现场维持秩序的警员介绍，周边四十多条道路已实施临时交通管制，除救援车辆外，社会车辆一律禁行。
大埔宏福苑外围 郑晨烨/摄
在封锁线外围，记者脚下的柏油路面上散落着大量黑色的颗粒状物体，一位警员告诉记者，这些都是从火场飘落并冷却后的“焦炭”，即被烧毁的建筑外墙残骸。
空气中弥漫着一股刺鼻的、混合着塑料与竹木烧焦的化学气味。
记者在封锁线外看到，整个屋苑的火势呈现出截然不同的两面，西北侧的大厦已经熄灭，隐入黑暗，只留下外墙大面积的熏黑痕迹。
而东南侧的三栋住宅楼，大火仍在持续，火焰不仅在外立面燃烧，更从多个高层单位的窗户内向外喷涌，被烧断的竹棚和杂物带着火星，不断从高空坠落至地面。
在警戒线内，停满了红色的消防车和白色的救护车，车顶的警示灯将街道映成一片红蓝交织的颜色，虽然特区政府通报显示已投入超过1200名消防及救护人员，但在火场核心区，物理条件的限制成为救援的最大掣肘。
记者在现场观察到，尽管多辆配备旋转台钢梯的重型消防车正在作业，但其喷射的水柱仅能覆盖楼宇的中低层区域，对于燃势猛烈的高层单位，地面的水龙明显“鞭长莫及”。
现场一位警务人员向记者确认，受限于现场街道的宽度以及现有消防设备的臂长，水枪和云梯确实难以直接触及顶层火点，目前的作业重点主要是对中层及外墙进行喷淋降温。
在夜空中，有几架隶属于消防处的无人机在被烟雾笼罩的大厦顶部盘旋，进行火场勘察和照明。
在封锁线外，记者遇到了多位已从火场撤离或正在等待消息的宏福苑居民，他们大多神情疲惫，衣着单薄。
一位住在宏昌阁9楼的罗姓居民告诉记者，火灾发生于下午两三点左右。
据他描述，起火点位于大厦底部的外墙棚架，火势是“从下往上”迅速烧起来的。
宏福苑建于1983年，楼龄超过40年，是香港早期的“居者有其屋”计划屋苑，社区内居住着大量长者。一位已经在宏福苑居住了三十多年的老街坊表示，由于大厦楼龄高，很多住户都是行动不便的老人，火灾发生速度之快，让高层住户几乎没有反应时间。
“没有听到警铃响。”这是记者在现场走访时，多位不同楼栋的居民共同提及的一个细节。
上述9楼居民回忆，事发时他并没有听到大厦的火灾警报声。
而他之所以能及时逃生，是因为手机上的社区群组里有人发消息说“着火了”，紧接着邻里之间开始“人传人”地互相通知。另一位逃生者也向记者证实，当时场面一度非常混乱，大家主要靠手机互通消息，或者看到窗外飘落的火星和浓烟才意识到危险迫近。
凌晨2时许，记者来到了位于中华基督教会冯梁结纪念中学的临时庇护中心。
学校的礼堂被临时征用，地上铺设了防潮垫和床褥，堆放着由香港民政事务处和社会福利署调配的饮用水、干粮和毛毯。
中华基督教会冯梁结纪念中学的临时庇护中心 郑晨烨/摄
庇护中心内虽然物资供应充足，但几乎没有人入睡。
居民们三三两两地围坐在一起，大部分人手里紧紧攥着手机，不断刷新新闻页面或接打电话，现场警方告诉记者，官方已设立伤者查询热线，协助市民查询亲友下落。
对于这里的很多居民来说，这是一个不眠之夜。
在庇护中心外，一位裹着毛毯的老人望着宏福苑方向腾起的烟雾，对记者说：“住了几十年，没见过这么大的火，希望火能尽快被扑灭，希望楼里的街坊邻居都能平安。”
“不寻常”的蔓延
宏福苑的大火之所以在短时间内演变成一场“重大灾难”，目前核心诱因指向了包裹着大厦外墙的维修工程物料。
据记者了解，事发的宏福苑楼龄已达42年。
根据宏福苑业主立案法团的会议记录，该屋苑于去年1月通过了一项总值约3.3亿港元的维修方案，主要工程包括外墙重修，承建商为宏业建筑工程有限公司，事发时，屋苑的多栋大厦外立面搭建了密集的竹制脚手架，并覆盖着绿色的尼龙防护网。
现场多位目击者向经济观察报记者描述了火势失控的过程。

在11月27日凌晨的记者会上，香港特区政府保安局局长邓炳强明确指出，消防人员在灭火过程中发现，大厦外墙的保护网、防水帆布以及一些塑胶布，在遇火后的蔓延程度“远比合规物料猛烈”，蔓延速度也明显较快。

这在一定程度上解释了为何火势会从单纯的外墙棚架火灾，演变为多层住宅内部同时起火的复杂局面。

李家超表示：“如有任何情况，我们会依法、依规追究责任。”

1 dead, 14 injured as massive fire rips through Bronx high-rise
- One person died and more than a dozen others were hospitalized after a gas explosion sparked a massive fire in a Bronx high-rise building, leading to a tragic incident that left residents shouting for help and firefighters performing dangerous operations on upper floors.
NEW YORK — One person died and more than a dozen others, including a firefighter, were hospitalized after a massive fire, sparked by a gas explosion, tore through the top of a Bronx high-rise early Saturday, officials said.
The four-alarm blaze broke out on the top floors of the 17-story Bivona Street building near Reeds Mill Lane in the Baychester neighborhood of the Bronx just before 12:15 a.m.
As heavy flames blew out windows, trapped residents were seen shouting for help as their neighbors scrambled downstairs, escaping the heavy smoke.
"It was really bad. The flames were just going up," Delores Singleton, 49, told the Daily News Saturday. "You could see people hanging out of windows begging for their lives, (screaming,) 'Help me! Help me!'"
Singleton, a nurse, was just about to make a late-night snack just after midnight when she "heard a big boom," she remembered.
"It shook the side of the living room," she said as she stood outside her building in the subfreezing temperatures Saturday morning. "I just ran out of the house. I had no warm clothes. My neighbors gave me what I have on right now."
In her mad dash to escape, she left behind her two parakeets — a gift from a patient. She was worried about their welfare on Saturday.
"I hope they can get them back to me," she said.
The New York City Fire Department was investigating a smell of gas on the 15th and 16th floors of the building, when "an explosion occurred," FDNY Chief of Department John Esposito said early Saturday.
"We had severe structural damage in six apartments on each floor. We eventually had fire in five apartments on the 16th floor and five apartments on the 17th floor," Esposito said. "It was a very, very dangerous operation for our firefighters, who performed incredibly on those upper floors, searching and protecting civilian life."
The building is part of the Boston Secor Houses. The complex was once run by NYCHA, but was recently taken over by a private company, which now runs the buildings, officials said.
While an exact cause for the blast was not immediately disclosed, neighbors suspected that an ongoing renovation project at the complex may have led to the explosion and fire.
Last week an electrical fire broke out in another building in the development, neighbors said.
Beacon Communities, the current managers of Boston Secor called the fatal fire a "tragic incident."
"Our thoughts are with everyone at the property, including residents and emergency response personnel, who have been affected," the company said in a statement. "We are actively gathering the necessary information to determine the cause of this incident. We are continuing to coordinate with our partners across the city, including emergency responders, to place all remaining residents in hotel rooms as quickly as possible."
Multiple residents recalled smelling gas before the explosion and raging inferno began.
"They (FDNY) checked our neighbor's oven because the neighbor's oven smelled like heavy gas. It smelled like it had a leak coming through. It smelled so potent," Cearia Marshall, 26, who lives on the 15th floor, recalled. "(We) called the Fire Department. They came, turned it off. Left. Building blew up."
"We started running down the stairs," she said.
Photos and video taken at the scene showed heavy flames shooting out of bay windows on the upper floors.
One tenant died at the the scene as firefighters doused the flames. A second tenant was rushed to Jacobi Medical Center with critical injuries.
The deceased tenant, who lived on the 17th floor, had not been immediately identified Saturday, officials said.
"Older gentleman, father, husband, (had) about three kids," tenant Kimberly Collins said, describing her deceased neighbor. "This is a horrible tragedy. You wouldn't want to wish this on anybody at all. We can't change back the hand of time, but somebody needs to be held accountable for this."
FedEx worker Jason Bueno, 27, was in his 12th-floor apartment when he heard the explosion above him.
"I heard a boom. I was up and it sounded loud so I went inside and got my mom and everybody and we started going down the stairs," Bueno said. "I thought the building was coming down."
Antionne Richardson had just returned home from his job as a security guard when he heard a big commotion outside in his 14th-floor hallway.
"At first, I didn't pay that any mind. I was minding my business," he said. "Then I heard a boom and it shook the building."
Richardson, 43, opened his apartment door and saw "everybody in the hallway."
"They said, 'Fire! You gotta leave!' so I got my whole family up and got them ready," he recalled.
As his family prepared to move, Richardson saw the firefighters coming up and showed them where the water pipe for the floor was.
"They said the smoke wasn't that bad and we didn't have to evacuate. But then about 10 minutes later they were, like, 'Everybody evacuate the building!' Everybody was taking the stairs. The people with wheelchairs, the FDNY was carrying them down."
A dozen tenants and a firefighter were taken to area hospitals with non-life-threatening injuries, the FDNY said. Another injured tenant refused medical attention.
Early radio reports stated the top of the building had been "blown off" and that people were trapped in their burning apartments.
More than 230 firefighters and EMS personnel raced to the scene to put out the massive conflagration and care for the injured. The fire was brought under control just before 5 a.m.
Multiple city agencies and the Red Cross were on the scene to care for civilians left outside in the frigid 10-degree weather, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said.
"I am with families at a nearby reception center, and we are working with the Red Cross to support displaced residents," Mamdani posted on X. "The fire is under control, but searches, inspections and utility restoration are ongoing."
At an unrelated press conference Saturday morning, Mamdani said that all of the building's 148 units had been evacuated.
"I visited residents there this morning," Mamdani said. "I hugged the woman in whose apartment that fire began. I could smell the fire still on her clothes. She was crying as she was mourning everything that she had lost. As you can imagine, this has been a deeply frightening and devastating morning. They are not alone. Our city will stand by them and do everything in our power to help them get back on their feet."
By 1:30 p.m., the Red Cross had cared for 101 households displaced from the fire. A total of 305 people, including 89 children, were asking for emergency assistance at a reception area on Reeds Mill Lane.
On Saturday afternoon, a Beacon Communities spokeswoman said, "Our priority right now is ensuring the households that are still impacted have a warm place to stay tonight and as long as necessary until they can return to their homes."
"The fire itself impacted 133 households in one building," she said. "However, residents in the other buildings were impacted for a period of time today as emergency personnel assessed the overall safety of the entire campus.
"At this time, all but the original 133 households that were directly impacted by the incident have been allowed to return to their homes, and partners are working now on placing those 133 households in hotels or ensuring they have alternate places to stay."
One displaced resident, who only identified himself as Horace, said he hadn't been allowed back in his apartment all day. He was not sure how he was going to survive Sunday's snowstorm under those conditions.
"I can't get into my house to get my clothes…They ain't telling nobody nothing. They just not letting people into the building," the 60-year-old tenant said. "We got a f—ing snowstorm about to go off in the city. You're just gonna displace people at this time when there's supposed to be inches of snow?"
FDNY fire marshals are trying to determine what initially sparked the gas explosion and fire, Esposito said. City officials believe that a boiler in the building exploded, but an official cause has not been determined.
"(We will be looking) into every single detail about this morning's fire," Mamdani said.
中文正文:
布朗克斯高层大火造成1人死亡，14人受伤
——纽约布朗克斯一栋高层住宅楼发生燃气爆炸引发大火，造成1人死亡，十多人住院，这一悲惨事件导致居民大喊求救，消防员在高层进行危险作业。
纽约——官员说，周六凌晨，一场由燃气爆炸引发的大火席卷了布朗克斯一栋高层建筑的顶部，造成1人死亡，包括一名消防员在内的十多人住院。
这场四级火灾在凌晨12点15分刚过爆发于布朗克斯贝切斯特社区里兹米尔巷附近比沃纳街17层建筑的顶层。
当猛烈的火焰震碎窗户时，可以看到被困居民大喊求救，而他们的邻居争先恐后地下楼逃离浓烟。
"真的很糟糕。火焰一直在往上窜，"49岁的德洛丽丝·辛格尔顿周六告诉《每日新闻》。"你可以看到人们从窗户探出身来乞求活命，（尖叫着，）'救救我！救救我！'"
辛格尔顿是一名护士，午夜刚过正准备做夜宵，这时她"听到一声巨响"，她回忆道。
"震动了客厅的一侧，"她周六早上站在建筑外、气温低于冰点的情况下说。"我就跑出了房子。我没有暖和衣服。邻居给了我现在穿的这些。"
在疯狂逃生中，她留下了她的两只虎皮鹦鹉——一位病人送的礼物。周六她很担心它们的安危。
"我希望他们能把它们还给我，"她说。
纽约消防局局长约翰·埃斯波西托周六凌晨说，消防部门正在调查建筑15楼和16楼的煤气味，这时"发生了爆炸"。
"我们每层有六套公寓遭受严重结构损坏。最终16楼有五套公寓着火，17楼有五套公寓着火，"埃斯波西托说。"对我们的消防员来说这是非常非常危险的行动，他们在那些高层表现出色，搜索和保护平民生命。"
该建筑是波士顿塞科尔住宅的一部分。官员说，该小区曾由纽约市房屋局管理，但最近被一家私营公司接管，现在运营这些建筑。
虽然爆炸的确切原因尚未立即公布，但邻居们怀疑小区正在进行的翻新工程可能导致了爆炸和火灾。
邻居们说，上周该开发项目的另一栋建筑发生了电气火灾。
波士顿塞科尔的现任管理公司 Beacon Communities 称这场致命火灾为"悲惨事件"。
"我们与该物业的所有人同在，包括受到影响的居民和应急响应人员，"该公司在声明中说。"我们正在积极收集必要信息以确定这一事件的原因。我们继续与全市的合作伙伴（包括应急响应人员）协调，尽快将所有剩余居民安置在酒店房间。"
多名居民回忆在爆炸和熊熊烈火开始前闻到煤气味。
"他们（纽约消防局）检查了我们邻居的烤箱，因为邻居的烤箱闻起来有浓重的煤气味。闻起来像有泄漏。味道太浓了，"住在15楼的26岁的西阿里亚·马歇尔回忆道。"（我们）打电话给消防部门。他们来了，关掉了。走了。然后楼就炸了。"
"我们开始跑下楼梯，"她说。
现场拍摄的照片和视频显示，猛烈的火焰从高层的凸窗喷出。
一名租户在消防员灭火时当场死亡。第二名租户被紧急送往雅各比医疗中心，伤势危急。
官员说，周六尚未立即确认住在17楼的死者租户身份。
"年长的绅士，父亲，丈夫，（有）大约三个孩子，"租户金伯利·柯林斯描述她死去的邻居时说。"这是一场可怕的悲剧。你不会希望这种事发生在任何人身上。我们无法让时光倒流，但需要有人为此负责。"
27岁的联邦快递工人杰森·布埃诺听到上方的爆炸声时正在12楼的公寓里。
"我听到一声巨响。我醒着，声音很大，所以我进去叫上我妈妈和所有人，我们开始下楼梯，"布埃诺说。"我以为楼要塌了。"
安蒂万·理查森刚从保安工作回家，就听到14楼走廊外面有很大的骚动。
"起初，我没在意。我在忙自己的事，"他说。"然后我听到一声巨响，震动了建筑。"
43岁的理查森打开公寓门，看到"走廊里全是人"。
"他们说，'着火了！你得走！'所以我叫醒了全家人，让他们准备好，"他回忆道。
当家人准备离开时，理查森看到消防员上来，告诉他们楼层的水管在哪里。
"他们说烟没那么大，我们不用疏散。但大约10分钟后，他们就说，'所有人疏散建筑！'每个人都在走楼梯。坐轮椅的人，纽约消防局把他们抬下来。"
纽约消防局说，十多名租户和一名消防员被送往地区医院，伤势不危及生命。另一名受伤租户拒绝就医。
早期无线电报道称建筑顶部"被炸掉"，人们被困在燃烧的公寓里。
超过230名消防员和急救人员赶到现场扑灭大火并救治伤者。火灾在凌晨5点前得到控制。
市长佐赫兰·马姆达尼说，多个市政机构和红十字会在现场照顾在严寒的10度天气里被留在外面的平民。
"我在附近的接待中心和家庭在一起，我们正与红十字会合作支持流离失所的居民，"马姆达尼在X上发文。"火势已得到控制，但搜索、检查和公用设施恢复正在进行中。"
在周六上午一场不相关的新闻发布会上，马姆达尼说建筑的全部148个单元都已疏散。
"我今天早上去看望了那里的居民，"马姆达尼说。"我拥抱了火灾起源公寓的那位妇女。我还能闻到她衣服上的烟味。她在哭泣，哀悼她失去的一切。可以想象，这是一个令人深感恐惧和毁灭性的早晨。他们并不孤单。我们的城市将与他们站在一起，尽我们所能帮助他们重新站起来。"
到下午1点30分，红十字会已照顾了因火灾流离失所的101户家庭。共有305人，包括89名儿童，在里兹米尔巷的一个接待区寻求紧急援助。
周六下午，Beacon Communities的一位女发言人说，"我们现在的首要任务是确保仍受影响的家庭今晚以及在必要的时间内有一个温暖的地方住，直到他们能够返回家园。"
"火灾本身影响了一栋建筑中的133户家庭，"她说。"然而，今天有一段时间，其他建筑的居民也受到影响，因为应急人员评估了整个园区的整体安全。
"目前，除了最初直接受事件影响的133户家庭外，所有居民都已被允许返回家园，合作伙伴现在正努力将这133户家庭安置在酒店或确保他们有其他住处。"
一位只愿透露叫霍勒斯的流离失所居民说，他一整天都不被允许回到公寓。他不确定在这种情况下如何度过周日的暴风雪。
"我进不了房子拿衣服……他们什么都不告诉任何人。他们就是不让人进建筑，"这位60岁的租户说。"我们他妈要迎来一场暴风雪了。你就要在这个本应有几英寸雪的时候让人流离失所？"
埃斯波西托说，纽约消防局消防督察正试图确定最初是什么引发了燃气爆炸和火灾。市政官员认为建筑里的一个锅炉爆炸了，但官方原因尚未确定。
"（我们将调查）关于今天早上火灾的每一个细节，"马姆达尼说。

title: Just silence : Families mourn elderly loved ones after Hong Kong inferno
完整正文(原文):
The last message Chris Wong received from her 72-year-old mother was a kindly reminder to wrap up warm as colder temperatures hit Hong Kong.
A couple of hours after her post in the family WhatsApp group, the frail woman's high-rise apartment block was a towering inferno. She is among 200 people missing in a tragedy that has claimed at least 128 lives.
More than a third of the inhabitants of Wang Fuk Court, the subsidised housing complex that went ablaze on Wednesday, were over the age of 65, well above the 20% average across the densely packed city.
Alone on the 21st floor
Wong's mother, who had bad joints and trouble walking, was alone on the 21st floor of one of the seven towers engulfed in the city's worst fire in over 80 years.
"When the fire started I rushed over ... I could see the outside of our flat and it was covered with flames. There was fire everywhere," said Wong, huddled with her father and elder sister on plastic chairs in an evacuation shelter outside the smouldering towers on Thursday.
"I just stood there calling and messaging my mum, but there was just silence," she added, tearing up.
Chim, a woman in her late 60s who asked to be identified by her surname, was one of the lucky ones.
She was watching television with her husband in her 15th floor apartment when she heard a commotion outside. She cracked open the window to see the bamboo scaffolding in the next block ablaze and sparks floating towards her building in the wind.
"Fire! Quick, get out!" she recalled her neighbours shouting. She only had time to grab some cash and her walking stick before taking the elevator down to safety.
Home for more than 40 years
Outside, the elderly couple watched in horror as the apartment they had lived in for more than 40 years was slowly engulfed in flames.
“We came down and just watched the fire. We watched it burn. There was nothing else we could do, just watched and hoped it wouldn’t keep burning," Chim said.
The apartments, built in 1983, were part of an affordable housing scheme aimed at getting low income residents on the property ladder in one of the world's most expensive real estate markets.
Around 37% of the 4,643 residents in the complex are now aged 65 or above, realtor Centaline said, citing the latest census data.
Residents of the housing complex had for more than a year complained about fire hazards posed by the renovation works, a Reuters investigation found.
One flagged the difficulty elderly residents would face escaping if an accident occurred, while another said the foam panels that covered the windows would leave many elderly, alone and immobile, in darkness, according to a forum for residents on Facebook reviewed by Reuters.
Police said they had arrested three construction company officials on suspicion of manslaughter for using unsafe materials, including the flammable foam. The company has not responded to requests for comment. The Independent Commission Against Corruption arrested eight others on Friday.
'They didn't make it'
David Ho's 73-year-old ex-wife and his son who lived on a high floor of one of the towers are also among the missing, he told Reuters as he sat alone on a park bench staring at the burnt tower blocks on Friday. The last he heard from his son was on November 20, the son's birthday, when he wrote back "thanks dad".
"I'm a positive, carefree person. If this didn’t happen, I'd live happily. Before I'd go to elderly centres, and ride my bicycle everywhere but now I don’t want to do anything at all. I feel very sad," the 75-year-old pensioner said. "It’s clear they didn’t make it."
Michelle Liu, a volunteer counsellor, spent much of the day roaming parks and shelters around the burnt out buildings, offering support for families and the many elderly people impacted by the disaster.
"They were quite emotional, I realised sometimes that money is important to them, but more important is for someone to be there with them in this difficult time to accompany them," she said.
"The people here feel a little bit lost at the moment, especially the people that I talked to. They don't know what will happen to them."
Collecting clothing, bedding and medication
Some elderly residents queued at a medical station in a shelter for fresh supplies of medication for longer-term conditions including high blood pressure and diabetes, while others stocked up on free supplies offered by volunteers in an adjacent housing estate, including clothes and bedsheets.
Chris Wong said she stood for six hours just staring helplessly at the burning building and trying to reach her mother as the blaze raged.
"I felt completely helpless ... my mum couldn’t walk properly, she had bad joints in both her knees ... and there was no one to help her."
Her father, who was out when the tragedy struck, added: "We have heard nothing. We have to slowly accept the reality."
A police announcement on a loudspeaker in the evacuation centre called for relatives to go to a nearby community hall to identify bodies. Wong and her elder sister sobbed quietly.
中文正文:
克里斯·黄从72岁母亲那里收到的最后一条信息是一条温馨提醒，随着香港气温下降要穿暖和点。
她在家庭WhatsApp群里发消息几小时后，这位体弱妇女的高层公寓楼变成了 towering inferno。她是这场已造成至少128人死亡的悲剧中200名失踪者之一。
周三起火的资助住宅小区宏福苑超过三分之一的居民年龄超过65岁，远高于这个密集城市20%的平均水平。
独自在21楼
黄的母亲关节不好，走路困难，在这座城市80多年来最严重火灾中被吞噬的七座塔楼之一的21楼独自一人。
"火灾开始时我冲了过去……我能看到我们公寓的外面，被火焰覆盖。到处都是火，"黄说，周四她和父亲、姐姐挤在冒烟塔楼外一个疏散庇护所的塑料椅子上。
"我就站在那里给妈妈打电话发信息，但只有沉默，"她补充说，泪流满面。
一位要求以姓氏称呼的60多岁妇女钦是幸运者之一。
她正在15楼的公寓里和丈夫看电视，这时听到外面有骚动。她微微打开窗户，看到隔壁楼栋的竹脚手架着火了，火花随风飘向她的建筑。
"着火了！快，出去！"她回忆邻居们喊道。她只来得及拿些现金和拐杖，就乘电梯到了安全地带。
住了40多年的家
在外面，这对老年夫妇惊恐地看着他们住了40多年的公寓慢慢被火焰吞噬。
"我们下来就看着火。看着它烧。我们别无他法，只能看着，希望它不要继续烧，"钦说。
这些建于1983年的公寓是经济适用房计划的一部分，旨在让低收入居民在这个世界上最昂贵的房地产市场之一获得房产。
房地产中介中原地产引用最新人口普查数据说，该小区4643名居民中约37%现在年龄在65岁或以上。
路透社的一项调查发现，该住宅小区的居民一年多来一直投诉翻新工程带来的火灾隐患。
路透社查阅的一个脸书居民论坛显示，有人指出如果发生事故老年居民逃生将面临困难，另一个人说覆盖窗户的泡沫板会让许多独居、行动不便的老年人陷入黑暗。
警方说，他们已逮捕三名建筑公司官员，涉嫌使用包括易燃泡沫在内的不安全材料而过失杀人。该公司未回应置评请求。廉政公署周五又逮捕了八人。
"他们没能逃出来"
何大卫73岁的前妻和住在其中一座塔楼高层的儿子也在失踪者之列，周五他独自坐在公园长椅上盯着被烧毁的塔楼时告诉路透社。他最后一次收到儿子的消息是在11月20日儿子生日那天，儿子回复说"谢谢爸爸"。
"我是一个乐观、无忧无虑的人。如果这没发生，我会幸福地生活。以前我会去老人中心，到处骑自行车，但现在我什么都不想做了。我感到非常难过，"这位75岁的养老金领取者说。"很明显他们没能逃出来。"
志愿者咨询师米歇尔·刘花了大半天时间在被烧毁建筑周围的公园和庇护所里转悠，为家庭和许多受灾难影响的老年人提供支持。
"他们情绪很激动，我意识到有时钱对他们很重要，但更重要的是在这个困难时期有人陪伴他们，"她说。
"这里的人现在感觉有点迷茫，特别是和我谈过的人。他们不知道自己会发生什么。"
收集衣服、被褥和药品
一些老年居民在庇护所的医疗站排队领取高血压和糖尿病等长期疾病的新鲜药品，其他人则在邻近住宅小区志愿者提供的免费物资中储备，包括衣服和床单。
克里斯·黄说她站了六个小时，只是无助地盯着燃烧的建筑，在大火肆虐时试图联系母亲。
"我感到完全无助……我妈妈走路不太好，她两个膝盖关节都不好……而且没有人帮她。"
悲剧发生时不在家的她父亲补充说："我们什么消息都没听到。我们得慢慢接受现实。"
疏散中心里警方用扩音器宣布，要求亲属到附近的社区礼堂辨认尸体。黄和姐姐轻声抽泣。

title: Navi Mumbai Tragedy : Six Dead , Including Child And Teen , In Two Separate Fire
完整正文(原文):
Navi Mumbai: Six people, including a six-year-old girl and a 17-year-old college student, died of burns in two separate fire incidents in Navi Mumbai during the early hours of Tuesday. While four members of a family lost their lives in a midnight blaze at Raheja Residency in Vashi, a mother and daughter died in another fire that broke out just a few hours later in Kamothe.
Four Dead in Raheja Residency Fire, Vashi
The first fire was reported around 12:40 a.m. at Raheja Residency, Plot Nos. 48/24, 25, 26, Sector 14, Vashi. The blaze, which started on the 10th floor, spread rapidly to the 11th and 12th floors before being brought under control by the Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation (NMMC) Fire Department after nearly three hours.
Multiple fire tenders from Vashi, Nerul, Airoli, and Koparkhairane were deployed at the site.
“Four persons were found dead during the rescue operation, while around 10 to 15 others were safely evacuated,” said Purushottam Jadhav, Chief Fire Officer, NMMC. “The fire originated from a flat on the 10th floor, though the exact cause is under investigation.” Prima facie, a short circuit in the air conditioner of flat no. 1005 is suspected.
The deceased were identified as Vedika Sundar Balakrishnan (6), her parents Sundar Balakrishnan (44) and Pooja Rajan (39) from flat no. 1205, and Kamla Hiralal Jain (84), a bedridden senior citizen from flat no. 1005.
Firemen’s Heroic Rescue Efforts
“Our men went through the flames, risking their lives to pull out people. We had banged the doors of flat no. 1205, but there was no response. The family was inside the bathroom, which was not known to anyone,” said Jadhav. “Many were scared to step out, and we had to convince them to open the doors. One 21-year-old boy who had locked himself in the bathroom was rescued after much persuasion.”
The deceased Balakrishnan family reportedly died due to smoke inhalation, while Jain was charred to death as she could not be evacuated in time.
NMMC Commissioner Kailash Shinde visited the spot and met affected families. “The fire team reached immediately after receiving the 12:40 a.m. call, but the fire had already spread. The deceased family was found unconscious and rushed to the hospital but could not be saved. A complete fire safety audit will be conducted,” Shinde said.
Two Killed in Kamothe Fire Hours Later
Just a few hours later, around 6:02 a.m., another fire broke out at Ambe Shraddha residential building in Sector 36, Kamothe, under Panvel Municipal Corporation limits. The blaze, suspected to have started due to a short circuit, was followed by a cylinder blast that intensified the fire in a third-floor duplex flat.
Two residents Rekha Sisodia and her 17-year-old daughter Payal Sisodia were found dead on their bed.
“Based on the site condition, it appears the fire started at least 45 minutes before the cylinder blast,” said Praveen Bodake, Chief Fire Officer, CIDCO. “Cylinders usually explode only after prolonged exposure to heat. Both victims likely inhaled smoke and fell unconscious before being charred.”
Bodake also stated that the 12-storey building lacked proper fire safety measures and ventilation. Two other family members survived as they were away for work at the time of the incident.

title: 1 dead , 15 others injured in Eastchester , Bronx high - rise fire and explosion
完整正文(原文):
EASTCHESTER, Bronx (WABC) -- One person was killed and 15 other people were hurt after a high-rise fire in the Bronx.
Citizen App video from a wider angle showed the top floors of the building as they turned into an inferno.
The fire broke out early Saturday at 12:19 a.m. on Bivona Street between Reeds Mill Lane and Boston Road in Eastchester.
It started on the 15th floor of the Boston Secor Houses. The FDNY was on the scene at the time to investigate a possible gas leak in the
building.
Officials say work was being done in the building, but only on the facade.
The explosion occurred in the building about 15 minutes after emergency officials arrived on the scene.
Several apartments became fully engulfed in flames.
Residents were seen in the windows of the building and one man was even spotted dangling with his legs out of the building as he tried to escape the intense heat from the fire.
One person was killed, another suffered critical injuries.
"Me and my kids, we all were asleep, and then there was a big explosion. We had to come down 12 flights of stairs," a woman said. "You know, he's in a wheelchair, and I had to struggle down the stairs with my three kids. My neighbor is the one who helped me and I don't know when we'll be able to go back in the building."
Residents of the lower floors stayed in the building during the firefighting efforts, but have since been moved to a nearby school.
Mayor Mamdani met with residents of the building later Saturday morning.
"We've just come from meeting with the families affected by a fire. We are currently taking care of these families in coordination with the American Red Cross, providing them with food and blankets and looking to secure them shelter for this evening and the evenings to come," Mamdani said. "We also know that the current focus is not only an investigation into the source of the fire, but also to extract the 14 homebound residents that are currently in the building. As soon as that is done, there will be a structural test of the building to actually ensure that anyone can return back into it."

title: Two Bajan - New Yorkers die in fire
完整正文(原文):
Grief, shock and a deep sense of loss have gripped an East Flatbush community in the heart of Brooklyn after a deadly fire took the lives of two Bajans – a mother and her son.
Eighty-year-old Angela Griffith and her 59-year-old son Wayne Griffith, originally from Farm Road, St Peter, died in the multi-alarm blaze along Kingston Avenue Monday night.
As residents of the predominantly English-speaking Caribbean immigrant neighbourhood pick up the pieces of their daily lives they are also thanking God for being spared following the tragedy.
Reached at his office in Manhattan, Barbados’ Consul-General in New York, Lorenzo Harewood, told the DAILY NATION: “Words cannot describe the tragedy of the deaths of the mother and son.
“Our hearts and sympathy go out to their relatives, friends and acquaintances who are obviously feeling the deep loss of the two victims who in their diverse ways have contributed to the betterment of the neighbours and the two countries – Barbados and the United States.”
It is estimated that more than 100 000 Barbadians live in Brooklyn, many of them in the exact neighbourhood where the Griffiths died.
“I didn’t know them, but I once lived in that neighbourhood,” said a retired Bajan.
Ben Marakowitz Svigals, who lives on the third floor of the afflicted high-rise building said: “It is very tragic.”
It was particularly so, “especially when you know the people”, he told a television news channel.
Another resident recounted: “I open my door, and the hallway was filled with smoke. I realise, [My God, there is a fire! So, I grabbed my keys and tried to run out. I met some firefighters in the hallways; they were knocking on the door to alert people to get out.”
A New York City Fire Department official said they were called to the fire around 11 p.m. and found the building was ablaze. They pulled the two Bajans from the damaged structure and ambulances rushed them to nearby Kings County Medical Centre where doctors were unable to save them.
The fire department is investigating to determine the cause of the fire. ( TB)

title: New York apartment building partially collapses in suspected gas explosion
完整正文(原文):
Investigation under way after 17-story New York apartment block partially collapses in suspected gas blast
Residents were forced to flee as a high-rise apartment building in New York'sBronx borough partially collapsed following a suspected gas explosion.
The blast happened at YCHA's Mitchel Houses on Alexander Avenue just after 8am, according to ABC 7.
During a morning press conference, Mayor Eric Adams confirmed that there were no deaths or injuries as a result of the collapse.
First responders used dogs and drones to sift through the rubble to make sure no one was hurt down below. There have been no reports of injuries.
According to the New York Fire Department, a gas explosion caused an incinerator shaft attached to the building to collapse. The rest of the 17-story building appear to have been left unaffected. No damage has been reported to any of the apartments.
"The fact that half of the building is gone and you felt it, it's like, luckily, I asked somebody, I asked was anybody injured? No injuries occurred. Luckily, everybody was able to get out safe. But feeling it and the intensity, and going downstairs, you could barely go downstairs, everybody is trying to go downstairs. People were carrying babies, people got no shoes on, got no coats, no hats, it's cold outside," a resident told ABC7.
Adams said the city was still clearing the area and ensuring the building is safe, but said that residents will be allowed to return to their apartments once they finish their inspection.
In the meantime, traffic and pedestrian restrictions have been established near the site of the collapse while crews continue their work to ensure the site is safe. Adams asked that pedestrians avoid the collapse site.
Bronx Borough President Vanessa Gibson said the explosion happened in the building's boiler room.
"There were no fatalities and no injuries as we have learned that this happened in the boiler room," she said at the news conference.
The mayor said an investigation into the cause of the collapse is ongoing.
A neighbor who had called the city to report seeing smoke near the building witnessed the explosion and subsequent collapse.
"I was explaining to the lady what I saw, and she was like, 'Hold on, let me transfer you to the fire department,'" she told WCBS. "Before she was about to do the transfer, the whole building just – you heard a loud boom, and the thing just exploded. And it fall down just like that."
Another resident told ABC 7 that the explosion sounded "like a bomb."
"My mom came knocking on my door and we ran out as soon as we could. I had no shoes on, but it sounded very urgent," a third resident said.
In addition to. the FDNY and the NYPD, the city's Buildings Department and the Department of Environmental Protection responded to the scene. Investigators determined that the explosion also destroyed an underground water main.
Con Edison has shut off gas to the site while crews continue their work.

title: Fire at luxury residential building in Tollygunge , several film stars come do
完整正文(原文):
Fire at luxury residential building in Tollygunge, several film stars come down onto street
Kolkata: A fire broke out in a luxury residence in the Tollygunge area of south Kolkata on Sunday afternoon, causing several Bengal film industry luminaries, who stay there, to come out onto the street below.
However, no injuries were reported in the incident, which covered the multi-storey building in black smoke.
The fire broke out in Tower 2 of Diamond City Residence, where several stars, including film couple Yash and Nusrat, actress and Trinamool Congress MLA Sayantika Banerjee, have flats.
It was learnt that Yash and Nusrat came down with their children in panic. The residents have been evacuated to a safe place.
Four fire engines were pressed into service after receiving the news.
Reports said that the fire broke out on the fifth floor. However, no one was in the room where the fire started. Initial estimates suggest that the fire started from a short circuit. The police and fire brigade were informed immediately and brought the situation under control.
While no one was injured in the incident, there are fears of a huge loss or damage to property. There are fears that if the fire had not been brought under control in time, it could have spread and caused a bigger accident.
The incident has spread panic among local residents.
When contacted, Banerjee said: “I heard about the fire breaking out in the residential building. However, I was not there at that time. I have come to the camp in Baranagar. I am fine.”
Director Shubhrajit Mitra, who also lives in that building, gave a detailed account of the incident.
“I heard that a Shivaratri puja was being held in the temple of a resident of the fifth-floor house. They lit a lamp and performed aarti. Without extinguishing the lamp, they came down, saying that they would perform the Shiva puja in the temple of the residence. In their absence, the fire probably caught fire from the lamp in the house.”
“I live on the 18th floor. My mother is sick at home. It took me a while to get down with her. Because the lift was closed. At that moment, I saw the rest of the residents of the building running down the stairs,” Mitra added.
Actor couple Yash and Nusrat’s flat is on the floor above the one where the fire broke out. Fearing for their lives, they immediately came down with their two children.
Two days ago, a fire broke out in the Globcine Crystal Building in Salt Lake Sector Five. A female employee of a multinational organisation fell ill due to the smoke. She was rescued and sent to the hospital.

title: Abbey View fire :  pure terror  as mum and daughter flee
完整正文(原文):
Watford Community Housing has been accused of "neglect" after a fire at Meriden flats put one person in hospital and left multiple homes uninhabitable.
Eight crews and police swarmed Abbey View on Saturday night (July 26) - three years on from a serious fire at the same 17-storey tower.
WCH said staff attended quickly to offer help and reassurance - with six households now in alternative accommodation - adding it will "continue to support all residents".
Sharonea Fitzgerald, who lives on the ninth floor with her six-year-old daughter, recalled "pure terror" as they tried to escape.
"It was just horrible," the 33-year-old told the Watford Observer. "I opened up my door and was greeted with thick black smoke, it was terrifying. My daughter is scared to be at home so I have had to drive her to my mum's house in Bournemouth and now I am in the flat alone."
She accused WCH of "neglect" over how quickly residents were allowed to return, adding: "I feel like they did not really test everything properly before letting everyone back in.
"The smell of smoke is so bad and they just sent us back home. They had cleaners do floors 11-17 the next day but did not do the downwards floors, so I have had to clean it myself."
Bemoaning the cost of ruined belongings, she said: "This is not the Hamptons, this is the Meriden, and I just feel so let down."
A WCH spokesperson said the fire service confirmed the building was safe for residents to return, with the worst-affected areas cleaned beforehand and a full deep-clean of all areas starting this week.
It comes just over three years after fire spread through the same building in July 2022 - which eventually saw boys aged 13 and 14 admit arson with recklessness as to whether life was endangered.
While the full report into the latest blaze has not yet been published, it is believed it may have been caused by a discarded cigarette.
  Dramatic Meriden tower video captures emergency services' fire response
  Meriden tower block fire: no criminal probe launched, police say
Sharonea said she feared "another Grenfell waiting to happen", although the Watford Observer understands the Meriden tower does not use the cladding present at Grenfell in 2017.
Other residents also voiced frustration on social media, with one writing: "This should not have happened, we had a serious fire only 3 years ago and some of us are still traumatised but yet have received no support or communication from WCH."
Another added: "Unbelievable that three years and two weeks since the last fire, it has happened again. Three years on, my girls and I are still not over it!"
The fire service confirmed eight engines were sent at around 10.20pm and smoke affected "multiple floors". Precautionary first aid checks were given to 13 people and one person was taken to hospital.
A spokesperson for WCH said: “We worked to support residents following the fire that occurred late on Saturday night – members of our team were quickly on site and remained there overnight and on Sunday to offer help and reassurance, working alongside local partners.
“Hertfordshire Fire and Rescue Service confirmed that the building was safe for residents to return. We carried out initial cleaning works to the worst-affected areas before allowing residents back into the block, and a full deep-clean of all areas will be carried out, starting this week, as well as decorative works.
“We also arranged alternative accommodation for six households whose front doors were damaged beyond repair by Hertfordshire Fire and Rescue Service during the evacuation. We will continue to support all residents by providing information and reassurance, and we would ask anyone who has concerns to contact us.”

沃特福德社区住房在梅里登公寓火灾致一人住院、多户住宅无法居住后被指控"疏忽"
周六晚上（7月26日），八支消防队和警察涌向阿比景观——距同一栋17层塔楼严重火灾已过去三年。
沃特福德社区住房说，工作人员迅速到场提供帮助和安慰——目前有六户家庭在替代住所——并补充说将"继续支持所有居民"。
沙罗妮娅·菲茨杰拉德和她6岁的女儿住在九楼，回忆起他们试图逃生时的"纯粹恐惧"。
"太可怕了，"33岁的她告诉《沃特福德观察家报》。"我打开门，迎面而来的是浓浓的黑烟，太可怕了。我女儿害怕待在家里，所以我不得不开车送她去伯恩茅斯我妈妈家，现在我一个人在公寓里。"
她指控沃特福德社区住房在允许居民返回的速度上"疏忽"，并补充说："我觉得他们在让每个人回来之前没有真正正确测试一切。
"烟味太浓了，他们就把我们送回家了。他们第二天让清洁工打扫了11-17楼，但没有打扫下面的楼层，所以我不得不自己打扫。"
她哀叹财物被毁的代价，说："这不是汉普顿，这是梅里登，我就是觉得太失望了。"
沃特福德社区住房发言人说，消防部门确认建筑对居民返回是安全的，受影响最严重的区域事先已清洁，所有区域的全面深度清洁本周开始。
这发生在2022年7月同一栋建筑火灾蔓延三年多之后——最终两名13岁和14岁的男孩承认鲁莽纵火，不顾是否危及生命。
虽然最新火灾的完整报告尚未发布，但据信可能是由被丢弃的香烟引起的。
沙罗妮娅说她担心"另一个格伦费尔正在等待发生"，尽管《沃特福德观察家报》了解到梅里登塔楼没有使用2017年格伦费尔存在的覆层。
其他居民也在社交媒体上表达了沮丧，一人写道："这不应该发生，我们三年前才发生过严重火灾，我们中的一些人仍然受到创伤，但却没有收到沃特福德社区住房的任何支持或沟通。"
另一人补充说："难以置信，距离上次火灾三年零两周，它又发生了。三年过去了，我和女儿们还没有走出来！"
消防部门确认晚上10点20分左右派出了八辆消防车，烟雾影响了"多个楼层"。对13人进行了预防性急救检查，一人被送往医院。
沃特福德社区住房发言人说："我们在周六深夜火灾发生后努力支持居民——我们的团队成员迅速到场，并在那里过夜和周日提供帮助和安慰，与当地合作伙伴合作。
"赫特福德郡消防救援局确认建筑对居民返回是安全的。在允许居民返回楼内之前，我们对受影响最严重的区域进行了初步清洁工作，所有区域的全面深度清洁将从本周开始进行，以及装饰工程。
"我们还为六户前门在疏散期间被赫特福德郡消防救援局损坏到无法修复的家庭安排了替代住所。我们将通过提供信息和安慰继续支持所有居民，并请任何有疑虑的人联系我们。"

荔湾区金兰苑小区的剑兰大厦，1994年建成，23层高楼三座塔楼住着近500户人家。从鞋柜、自行车、婴儿车，到花盆、废旧家具、纸箱泡沫……五花八门的物品长年侵占大部分楼道与楼梯间。 记者随机走进一栋塔楼，22层中有20层可见杂物堆积。约两米宽、7米长的楼道内，少则几辆自行车、几盆大型盆景，多则各种杂物占据了2/3的通道，不少已覆上一层厚厚的灰尘，可见堆积时日之久。 从三楼顺着疏散通道往上，有的楼层并未安装照明设施，需要打开手电才方便行走。到了四层与五层，疏散通道堆满酒店使用的布草、塑料桶、垃圾车，以及储物柜等大件物品，不仅影响消火栓开启，也阻碍了疏散通道的正常出入。 在尚德大厦，疏散通道随意堆放的柜子等大件物品，将消火栓掩在了背后。 更严重的是，尽管贴有禁止吸烟的标语，仍有部分人员将消防通道视为吸烟场所。记者注意到，在堆放泡沫箱的角落地面，有多个烟头。 Bristol council apology after over-60s 'stuck inside tower block behind broken door'
"This created a serious risk"
Council chiefs have apologised to residents of an over-60s tower block in South Bristol, after it took three days to fix the front door, leaving some elderly people inside unable to get out of the building. A formal complaint has been submitted by the tenants’ representative of the tower block, saying the council left many in the building in a potentially dangerous situation for days.
Residents at Gilton House in Brislington first began reporting that the electric-powered mechanism on the only door out of the building had failed at around 3pm last Tuesday (July 1).
It meant the door had to be opened manually, by over-riding the mechanism by force - something many residents couldn’t do, leaving them unable to get out of the building or calling on neighbours for help. Nigel Varley, who lives in the block and is the residents’ rep, said that was a potentially dangerous situation.
“The door had to be pushed open,” he said. “It is very stiff and some of our residents with limited mobility found this either very difficult or impossible. Also, if the door-opening button was pushed, the door jammed until the electric motor stopped working,” he added.
“This created a serious risk. If a fire had broken out and people evacuated, perhaps in smoke, the difficulty in opening the door would have created panic and possibly trapped people inside.
“There is another fire escape but that is in the community room which is kept locked so residents evacuating in a hurry who left their key behind could not use it,” he claimed. However, the council said it is "confident that there was no adverse impact on any tenant’s ability to evacuate the building".
Residents of Gilton House began to call Bristol City Council that Tuesday afternoon but said it was a challenge to persuade the city council of the seriousness of the situation.
“The caller had difficulty in persuading the operator that it was an emergency with danger to life,” said Mr Varley. “In a tower block with one entrance/exit and older residents, it should have been obvious that this posed a danger. We were told that someone would be out to fix it 'that night' but no-one came,” he added.
Various people did come and go with failed attempts to fix the door over the rest of last week, and at one point the door was left unlocked, which concerned residents too.
“This removed security from the block in the week when we had intrusion by teenagers who tried doors and smoked dope in the foyer until a resident chased them off,” said Mr Varley.
By Thursday, residents called Avon Fire and Rescue to come, because they feared the building was now a fire hazard, but all they said they could do was call the council themselves to urge them to fix the door.
“A member of the council’s repairs team came on Thursday afternoon,” said Mr Varley. “He spent a long time on the phone trying to arrange a repair but left saying someone 'might' be there by 6pm. No-one came,” he added.
“A contractor arrived early on the morning of Friday July 4, and repaired both the door and the entry camera. This has not worked for many weeks and is an essential part of the block's security.
“It has taken two and more days to repair a serious and potentially dangerous fault in our one and only block entrance door. This episode raises a number of serious issues.
“The delay in repairing the front door to Gilton House placed us and every other resident at risk,” he said. “Gilton House has 46 flats and only one entry door. It is supported housing for the over-60s and has a number of residents with very limited mobility.
“In spite of the aftermath of the Grenfell Tower tragedy, and the many policy papers and discussions on fire safety by Bristol City Council, there are still flaws in its ability to recognise and respond to situations which put its tenants at risk,” he said.
“There is a failure to take into account the special needs of older and disabled people. This is not the first time we have experienced discrimination,” he claimed.
“The repairs team does not seem to have on hand the resources to respond quickly to situations such as ours. There is a reliance on contractors who can dictate the timescale,” he added.
The man in charge of housing in Bristol, Cllr Barry Parsons, the chair of the homes and housing delivery committee, apologised ‘for any inconvenience’, but said because the door could be opened, it was not deemed an emergency.
“Our repairs and maintenance team aim to complete any repairs or issues raised as quickly as possible to minimise disruption to tenants,” said Cllr Parsons (Green, Easton). “We apologise for any inconvenience caused to residents while the door was not fully operational.”
“Residents’ safety is always our priority and we are confident that there was no adverse impact on any tenant’s ability to evacuate the building while repairs were ongoing. Emergency exits are also available within the building in the community room, the tenant storage room, and the office, to ensure a safe and efficient evacuation if needed,” he added.
The council said the repair required visits from ‘multiple teams as differing specialisms were required and a part was required to be ordered’.
“A broken door does not fall under an emergency which requires repairs within a day because it can be operated manually,” a spokesperson added.

布里斯托尔议会就60岁以上老人'被困在破损门后的塔楼'道歉
"这造成了严重风险"
议会负责人已向布里斯托尔南部一栋60岁以上塔楼的居民道歉，因为花了三天时间才修好前门，导致一些里面的老年人无法走出建筑。该塔楼的租户代表已提交正式投诉，称议会让建筑里的许多人在潜在危险的情况下待了几天。
布里斯灵顿吉尔顿楼的居民上周二（7月1日）下午3点左右首次开始报告，建筑唯一出口的电动机构失灵了。
这意味着门必须手动打开，通过用力覆盖机构——许多居民做不到，导致他们无法走出建筑或呼吁邻居帮助。住在楼里并担任居民代表的奈杰尔·瓦利说，这是一个潜在危险的情况。
"门必须被推开，"他说。"它非常僵硬，我们一些行动不便的居民发现这要么非常困难要么不可能。此外，如果按下开门按钮，门会卡住直到电动马达停止工作，"他补充说。
"这造成了严重风险。如果发生火灾，人们疏散，也许在烟雾中，开门的困难会造成恐慌，并可能将人困在里面。
"还有另一个消防出口，但那在社区室里，一直锁着，所以匆忙疏散忘记带钥匙的居民无法使用它，"他声称。然而，议会说它"确信没有对任何租户疏散建筑的能力产生不利影响"。
吉尔顿楼的居民周二下午开始打电话给布里斯托尔市议会，但说要说服市议会情况的严重性是一个挑战。
"打电话的人很难说服接线员这是危及生命的紧急情况，"瓦利先生说。"在只有一个入口/出口且居民年长的塔楼里，这应该很明显构成了危险。我们被告知有人会'那天晚上'来修，但没有人来，"他补充说。
上周剩下的时间里，各种人来来去去，试图修门都失败了，有一次门被留着没锁，这也让居民担心。
"这在一周内取消了楼的安全保障，当时我们有青少年闯入，他们试门并在门厅吸大麻，直到一位居民把他们赶走，"瓦利先生说。
到周四，居民打电话给埃文消防救援局来，因为他们担心建筑现在是火灾隐患，但他们说他们所能做的就是自己打电话给议会敦促他们修门。
"议会维修团队的一名成员周四下午来了，"瓦利先生说。"他花了很长时间打电话试图安排维修，但离开时说有人'可能'会在下午6点前到。没有人来，"他补充说。
"一名承包商于7月4日周五一早到达，修好了门和入口摄像头。这已经很多周不能用了，是楼安全的重要组成部分。
"花了两天多时间才修复我们唯一楼入口门的一个严重且潜在危险的故障。这一事件引发了一些严重问题。
"修复吉尔顿楼前门的延误使我们和其他所有居民处于危险之中，"他说。"吉尔顿楼有46套公寓，只有一个入口门。它是60岁以上老人的支持性住房，有许多行动非常不便的居民。
"尽管有格伦费尔塔悲剧的后果，以及布里斯托尔市议会关于消防安全的许多政策文件和讨论，它在识别和响应使租户处于危险的情况方面仍然存在缺陷，"他说。
"没有考虑到老年人和残疾人的特殊需求。这不是我们第一次经历歧视，"他声称。
"维修团队似乎没有手头的资源来快速响应我们这样的情况。依赖可以决定时间尺度的承包商，"他补充说。
布里斯托尔负责住房的人，住房和住房交付委员会主席巴里·帕森斯议员，为"任何不便"道歉，但说因为门可以打开，所以不被视为紧急情况。
"我们的维修和维护团队旨在尽快完成任何维修或提出的问题，以尽量减少对租户的干扰，"帕森斯议员（绿党，伊斯顿）说。"我们为门未完全运行期间给居民造成的任何不便道歉。"
"居民的安全始终是我们的首要任务，我们确信在维修进行期间没有对任何租户疏散建筑的能力产生不利影响。建筑内的社区室、租户储藏室和办公室也有紧急出口，以确保在需要时安全高效地疏散，"他补充说。
议会说，维修需要"多个团队访问，因为需要不同的专业知识，并且需要订购一个零件"。
"破损的门不属于需要在一天内维修的紧急情况，因为它可以手动操作，"发言人补充说。
